decisions.summary: rollback_sensitive axis: the change set reverts atomically; feature-gate and upgrade/downgrade legs are non-applicable to an additive ledger file plus a test-pin realignment
decisions.reason: Rollback plan: the entire PR (ledger commits + pin commit bb1a463f) reverts with git revert of the set; no migration, no schema change, no dependency change. Stored-object safety: the only new stored object is .vibepro/reviews/<story>/surface-violations.json, which is additive-only, is read clean when absent, and whose corrupt/truncated states fail closed with a typed error, so a revert leaves no unreadable state behind. Version skew: an older vibepro binary running against a repo that already has a ledger file simply never reads it (the file is namespaced under .vibepro/reviews and old readers do not reference it), degrading to pre-ledger behavior without error; a newer binary against a repo without a ledger reads clean by design (AC-7). Feature gate: none exists and none is required - the gate blocks only on unacknowledged violations, and repos with no violations see a passed gate, so disabled-behavior testing has no subject. Upgrade/downgrade test: non-applicable for the same reason; the acceptance suite already covers the legacy-artifact leg (RSV-7 legacy lifecycles read clean). The npm-side rollback path for the version pin is owned by docs/specs/story-vibepro-release-0-2-0-beta-2.md Operations and unchanged here.

decisions.summary: release_ops axis activated by the version-pin realignment commit bb1a463f; no new operator or user action is introduced by this PR
decisions.reason: The release_ops axis fired because the diff now touches test/public-release-notes.test.js. That commit only realigns the hardcoded npm dist-tag expectation (0.2.0-beta.1 -> 0.2.0-beta.2) with the registry state published by merged PR #396, repairing main's own red CI (same cross-PR pin-conflict class as the /pass 18 -> 19/ correction shipped in #396). The operator path for the release itself is owned and documented by the release story: CHANGELOG 0.2.0-beta.2 is the release note authority, and docs/specs/story-vibepro-release-0-2-0-beta-2.md Operations documents rollout (post-merge workflow), rollback (npm deprecate + dist-tag repoint to beta.1 + revert main before any workflow re-run), and observability (workflow run log, GitHub Release, npm view vibepro version). This PR adds no operator action, no release note obligation beyond the already-merged one, and no support path change; the ledger feature itself ships inside the normal package release train. Owner-visible evidence: npm view vibepro dist-tags returns latest=0.2.0-beta.2 beta=0.2.0-beta.2, matching both docs/*/reference/version-history.md tables and the updated pin.

decisions.summary: Bug physics selected the deployment class from a Japanese keyword; the version-stamp probe it asks for is this Story's actual mechanism
decisions.reason: The deployment class was selected because the Story text repeatedly says 'レビュー実行中' and the classifier matches the substring 実行中. This Story is not a deployment fix and ships no artifact-versioning change, so that label should not be read as one. The probe the deployment profile asks for - evidence that the running session reads the expected artifact version - is nevertheless satisfied on its merits rather than by coincidence: review close records closed_head_sha and closed_surface_digest as the running review session's stamp of the surface it actually read, compares that stamp against the start-time stamp instead of assuming they agree, and RSV-8 reconciles the lifecycle pointer against the ledger entry so a substituted artifact version is reported rather than trusted. The recorded evidence is the unit run's version_stamp scenario at the current head, not a text match. A reviewer should read this gate as covered by that mechanism, not as a claim that a deployment bug was diagnosed and fixed.

decisions.summary: One reviewable unit: the new ledger module, the call sites that consume it, its gate node and its tests are a single contract
decisions.reason: The diff is one decision read end to end: src/review-surface-violations.js is the only new module, and src/agent-review.js, src/independent-review-orchestrator.js, src/pr-manager.js and src/cli.js each touch it for the same reason - record the close-time snapshot, append the typed entry, surface it as gate:review_surface_integrity, and expose it read-only on the CLI. Splitting would leave a gate reading a ledger no writer maintains, so the blast radius is deliberately bundled and is bounded by the design root's owned surfaces. Review ownership is the gate stage: gate_evidence owns the gate node and the evidence shape, release_risk owns the operational exit. The remaining review_owner_map evidence is produced by that pending gate-stage agent review and is dispatched separately; it is not waived here. What is decided here is only the scope question - this PR is one reviewable unit and is not to be split.
